fatal_errors: The proposed composition change does not reconstruct the relevant HEBM-plus-SPS intervention or its nanocrystalline FCC/BCC structural mediator.
The claim that equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has minimal atomic-size mismatch is unsupported and questionable because Ti is substantially size-mismatched with the other constituents.
Replacing Co with Al changes chemical bonding, phase stability, stacking-fault behavior, and potentially precipitation, so it does not isolate lattice distortion as the causal variable.
No prior evidence is identified despite the explicit requirement to support the mechanistic premise.
The processing window, exact modified composition, SPS conditions, milling conditions, and quantitative mechanical predictions are absent.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the qualitative strength–ductility tradeoff and proposes measurable comparisons and a falsification rule, but it is not a reconstruction of the target mechanism. The target attributes strengthening primarily to HEBM-induced nanocrystallinity, accumulated defects, solid-solution strengthening, densification, and an approximately 83% FCC/17% BCC structure retained after SPS. The generated answer instead changes alloy chemistry and assigns causality to lattice distortion. Its comparison is substantially confounded because Al substitution can alter phases and bonding even if obvious secondary phases are not detected. It also misses the target processing conditions and quantitative outcomes of about 675 HV, 1894 MPa compressive strength, 1238 MPa yield stress, and greater than 6.5 g/cm³ density. Consequently, it is testable in a broad sense but lacks evidentiary support and does not adequately isolate its claimed mechanism.
